subject: business-studies
title: Ratio Analysis Overview
welcome_lead: Compress whole accounts into a handful of decisive ratios.
meta_desc: A-Level Finance: liquidity, profitability, gearing and efficiency ratios.
final_note: Ratios are signals, not verdicts - always compare across years and rivals.

concepts.def: Current assets divided by current liabilities.
(Current assets minus stock) divided by current liabilities.
Operating profit divided by capital employed, expressed as a percentage.
Gross profit as a percentage of revenue.
Net profit as a percentage of revenue.
Long-term debt as a share of total capital employed.

walkthroughs.body_html: Current ratio = CA / CL. A figure around 1.5 to 2 is typical. Acid test strips out stock - for stock-heavy retailers it can dip below 1 safely.
ROCE = operating profit divided by capital employed, times 100. It shows how efficiently capital is converted into operating profit and is a key signal for investors.
Gearing = long-term liabilities divided by (capital + long-term liabilities), times 100. Above 50 percent is highly geared - interest costs can swamp profits in a downturn.

options: Current assets divided by current liabilities
Operating profit divided by capital employed
Return earned on the capital invested in the business
